title: Move the market

readouts.v: {abs(gap)<1 ? "no gap" : (gap>0 ? "excess demand of " + fmt(gap,0) : "excess supply of " + fmt(-gap,0))}

predict.q: A heatwave makes ice cream more popular. What happens to the price and quantity of ice cream sold?

options.fb: Demand shifts right. At the old price there is excess demand, so the price rises and firms extend supply: both rise.
Price and quantity move in opposite directions only when supply shifts. Here demand shifted right, so both rise.
A lower price with more sold comes from an increase in supply. More demand pushes the price up.

options.s: Price rises, quantity stays the same
options.fb: When the price rises, firms extend supply, so more is sold. Quantity only stays the same if supply is perfectly inelastic.

task: Move the **demand** slider to the right and watch Pe and Qe. Then move the **supply** slider both ways.

target.do: Move the demand slider to +100, then press Check.

takeaway: Find which curve moves first, then read the new crossing point.
explore: Now shift supply each way: price and quantity move in opposite directions.

inv: abs(gap)<1 ? has(R2,'no gap') : (gap>0 ? has(R2,'excess demand') : has(R2,'excess supply'))
